# Free product systems not generated by their tensor core

**Status: claimed_solved, 3/5 author turns. Complete negative answer claimed for the exact generation question; independent automated audits passed their assigned scopes.** This is an AI-assisted mathematical result with no claim of external human peer review or established novelty.

Target: UnsolvedMath **30001179 / OWR-3392-005**, “Generation of Free Product Systems by Tensor Subsystems.” The original question appears in Michael Skeide's “Free Product Systems,” Oberwolfach Reports 6 (2009), pp.528–530, especially p.530: [official report](https://publications.mfo.de/bitstream/handle/mfo/3111/OWR_2009_09.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.4171/OWR/2009/09).

## Result and scope

The construction is a pointed free product system of separable complex Hilbert spaces, hence Hilbert C–C bimodules with central unit reference vectors. It has associative pointed bilinear free-product unitaries, the canonical zero-time fibre, and an explicit continuous-field structure with continuous multiplication.

Its maximal tensor subsystem is the time-ordered finite-word Fock system. The free subsystem generated by that tensor core contains exactly the finite words. A nonzero closed infinite-word sector remains orthogonal to that free hull, giving the claimed counterexample to universal generation. The proof computes the intersection directly rather than assuming a general Hilbert-module tensor/intersection theorem.

Read the [frozen proof](CANDIDATE_PROOF.md), followed by the [additive exposition note](EXPOSITION_NOTE.md). The construction is unchanged from the version reviewed by both independent audits.
